keyTerms: העשיר לא ירבה והדל לא ימעיט

252.title: A Person Must Recognize That His Desire and Generosity of Heart Likewise Derive From…
252.summary: One must recognize that even his desire and generosity come from Hashem (the Higher Unity), after which that desire becomes his permanent possession and his own Torah (the Lower Unity).
keyTerms: הקדוש ברוך הוא לבן של ישראל
כי ממך הכל ומידך נתנו לך
ברוך שם כבוד מלכותו לעולם ועד
הקדוש ברוך הוא גוזר וצדיק מבטל

253.title: Through the Generosity of Heart of the Children of Israel with Their Wealth (me'od)
253.summary: Generosity with wealth builds sanctity of place, with bodily action sanctity of time, and with the heart sanctity of soul, mirrored in Temple, Shabbat and leader, and in the three loves of the Shema.

topics.en: With All Your Heart, Soul and Might
topics.he: בכל לבבך ובכל נפשך ובכל מאדך

keyTerms: מי שטרח בערב שבת יאכל בשבת
בכל לבבך ובכל נפשך ובכל מאדך

254.title: A Person Must Offer Unto Hashem
254.summary: Serving with all one's heart, soul and might means subordinating what one is naturally bound to, as the Patriarchs' trials show; David's trial lay in insatiable desire, the yetzer's 'very good'.

255.title: Rectification Through the Opposite Extreme
255.summary: One deficient in a trait must rectify it by the opposite extreme even forgoing a mitzvah; Mordechai saved Ahasuerus to uproot the narrow eye, Persia's kelipah, which mishloach manot counters.

256.title: The Holy Spark Within Every Nation
256.summary: Every nation lives by a holy spark that Israel absorbs in exile; Esther drew Persia's modesty, enabling the Second Temple and a revelation that nature itself is Hashem's hidden guidance, opposed by shameless Amalek.

257.title: Israel's Holy Longing and the Spiritual Roots of the Nations
257.summary: Israel's root is longing for Hashem, the nations' root is worldly lust; the letters Kuf and Hei, Yosef and Adar, teach that desire is conquered by transforming it into longing for God.
keyTerms: הכל בידי שמים חוץ מיראת שמים

258.title: The Place of the Transgressor Within Israel
258.summary: As the community needs its transgressors, each person holds a necessary 'little folly'; by blessing permitted pleasures the evil side praises God and Nogah is absorbed, while lust is curbed on the middle path.

259.title: Faith as the Root of Every Good Thing
259.summary: Faith, Sinai's 'I am Hashem', is the root of all good, and mockery, Amalek's trait, the root of all evil; levity casts off the yoke and opposes prayer, David's rung of faith.

260.title: Two Forms of Laughter and Their Rectification
260.summary: Scornful laughter is permitted only toward idolatry, as on Purim, while playful laughter is permitted for a mitzvah, broadening the heart before study; God laughs over His creatures only in the future.

261.title: The Holy One, Blessed Be He, His Glory Fills the Whole Earth
261.summary: Hashem fills the earth in concealment; Avraham's burning palace was an unchanneled blaze of love until Torah and mitzvot gave it the bounded light of a lamp, as the Taberah complainers show.

262.title: The Essence of the Soul Is the Power of Life-vitality
262.summary: The soul is vitality clothed in thought, speech and action; its food is delight, found chiefly in Torah, while pleasure from sin must be purged by Gehinnom, suffering, or counterbalance repentance.

263.title: Thought, Speech, and Action of Torah and Mitzvot Are Garments of Honor for Man
263.summary: Torah and mitzvot in thought, speech and action are the soul's garments of honor; Torah's garments reveal inwardness and are received through fear, like the priestly garments that atone.

topics.en: Torah Not for Its Own Sake

264.title: Mockery as the Entryway into Evil
264.summary: Mockery, Amalek's root trait, is the entryway into all impurity and has no future; the High Priest's body and the incense altar's crown, Keter, rectify it and the hidden root of evil.
keyTerms: ארבע כתות שאין מקבלות פני שכינה
חנפים שקרנים מספרי לשון הרע ולצים
